## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column needs fixing before merge: it publishes the start time of processes that are still running and never reports a real finish time. Its documented NULL meaning also contradicts the rows the model produces.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` file at the repository root.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — finished_at holds the start time of running processes — For process 20, whose latest event is `started` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, `finished_at` returns that start time although the process has not finished. The CASE only matches `'started'`, and `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows no finish event type (`'created', 'started', 'cleared'`). — Consumers will read in-progress processes as finished at their start time, and no row ever gets a true finish timestamp. — Fix: Either rename the column to `started_at` and take `occurred_at` from the `started` event, or add a finish event type to the source and key the CASE on it.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — NULL meaning contradicts started-then-cleared processes — Process 30 was started (event 3) and then cleared (event 4), yet it gets `finished_at` NULL, while the docs say "NULL means the process has never been started." The CASE only looks at the latest event, so any process whose last event is not `started` gets NULL. — Consumers filtering on `finished_at IS NULL` will wrongly count started-and-cleared processes as never started.
